title: Even latria/dulia champions admit scriptural mix-up of the terms, yet defend the School distinction as anti-equivocation coinage
source_text: V. Imo illi ipsi qui hunc vocum Latriae & Duliae usum, prout in Schola Romana usurpantur, maxime probant, agnoscunt tamen voces illas apud profanos Scriptores, & in usu communi confundi: imo in sacra Scriptura apud Graecos interpretes; latreian quandoque dici de servitio humano: saepe vero tam in Novo quam in Veteri Testamento duleian pro cultu solius Dei summi. Veruntamen pertendunt Scholam Theologicam non sine causa excogitavisse distinctionem illam Latriae & Duliae. Nam cum in re inveniatur manifesta distinctio inter cultum Dei & Sanctorum, oportuisse etiam, ad vitandam aequivocationem, utrumque cultum distincto vocabulo designari. Nec sine ratione ad hoc delectas volunt Latriae & Duliae voces; quia latreia in Novo Testamento ad solum Dei cultum significandum adhibetur: duleia vero sumitur pro omni servitute tam Dei quam hominum. Quicquid vero de eo sit, quemadmodum licuit antiquae Ecclesiae contra Veteres haereticos nova invenire vocabula, ut voces homoousios, Trinitatis, &c. Sic etiam licuisse Ecclesiae Posteriori, contra Haereticos posteriores, vocabula quaedam nova invenire, aut saltem vocabulis antea usitatis in alia significatione uti.
pass_a_gloss: Nay, those very ones who most approve this use of the words Latria and Dulia as they are employed in the Roman School nevertheless acknowledge that those voices are confused among profane writers and in common use: nay, in sacred Scripture among the Greek interpreters; latreia is sometimes said of human service: but often both in the New and in the Old Testament duleia is taken for the cult of the one supreme God. Nevertheless they contend that the Theological School not without cause devised that distinction of Latria and Dulia. For since in the thing a manifest distinction is found between the cult of God and of the Saints, it was also necessary, to avoid equivocation, that each cult be designated by a distinct vocabulary. Nor without reason do they will the voices Latria and Dulia chosen for this; because latreia in the New Testament is applied to signifying the cult of God alone: but duleia is taken for every servitude both of God and of men. But whatever be of that, just as it was lawful for the ancient Church against the old heretics to invent new vocabularies, as the voices homoousios, of the Trinity, etc., so also it was lawful for the later Church, against later Heretics, to invent certain new vocabularies, or at least to use vocabularies formerly customary in another signification.
pass_b_english: Even latria/dulia partisans admit the Greek terms blur in pagan use and Scripture—latreia sometimes of human service, duleia often of God’s own cult.
They still defend the School coinage: the thing differs, so the names must, to kill equivocation.
As the old Church coined homoousios against heretics, so the later Church may rebaptize words against later errors.

choices.why: Keep Greek lemmas as the School’s contested pair.
